title: Integral fpqc descent with finite fibres and affine neighbourhoods
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning it has an affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. An fpqc sheaf means a contravariant set-valued functor on $S$-schemes satisfying the covering equalizer condition of [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Let $F$ be such a sheaf, and let $p:S^{\prime}\to S$ be an fpqc morphism such that $F_{S^{\prime}}$ is represented by a scheme locally of finite presentation over $S^{\prime}$. Suppose $q:T\to S$ is integral, surjective, flat and quasi-compact, with finite underlying fibres [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and $F_T$ is represented by a locally Noetherian scheme $Y$. Assume $Y$ has property (FA). Property (FA) means that every finite subset of the underlying point set is contained in an affine open subscheme. Then $F$ is represented by an $S$-scheme $X$ with property (FA). If $Y\to T$ is flat and separated and of finite presentation, so is $X\to S$. Flatness is [def-weil-flat-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Proposition 4.1.1 and Proposition 4.1.3 (scan OCR 4.1.5), printed pp.54-55: integral descent criterion and descent of affine neighbourhoods; restrict to integral covers which are also fpqc. Last property clause: Stacks Tags 02KU, 02L0, 02L2, descent.tex labels lemma-descending-property-separated, lemma-descending-property-finite-presentation, lemma-descending-property-flat. Local archive WANTED; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1973__33__5_0.pdf

proof.text: Choose representing identifications $h_P\simeq F_{S'}$ and $h_Y\simeq F_T$. On double overlaps both pullbacks represent the same restriction of $F$. By [lem-pc-representable-unique], the unique comparison respecting these identifications gives descent data on $P$ and $Y$. On triple overlaps both composites respect the same identification, which proves the cocycle. The base change $T\times_SS'\to T$ is fpqc. Over it, $Y$ is the base change of $P$ and hence locally of finite presentation. Descent of that property shows that $Y\to T$ is locally of finite presentation. This use of property descent is between existing schemes and makes no representability assumption about $F$ on $S$.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, canonical overlap schemes and data, p.16; Stacks descent.tex 02KY (lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-presentation)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-integral-descent-finite-point-orbits] to $q$, $Y\to T$ and its canonical datum: the cover has finite underlying fibres by hypothesis, and $Y$ is locally Noetherian by hypothesis. Thus for every $y\in Y$, the orbit $O_y=r_1(r_0^{-1}(y))$ is a finite subset of $Y$. Property (FA) supplies an affine open containing $O_y$. We use finiteness of this image, not the generally false assertion that finite underlying fibres of $q$ stay finite after every base change.

source.place: Finite-orbit prerequisite for Theorem 4.1(ii); agent expansion for the finite-underlying-fibre specialization

proof.text: The preceding orbit neighbourhoods meet precisely the hypothesis of [lem-sfb-integral-descent-invariant-quasiaffine-charts]. Its other hypotheses are the original fpqc sheaf $F$, the given locally finitely presented model $P$, the integral surjective cover $T\to S$, and the representing scheme $Y$. Obtain a covering $(U_i)$ of $P$ by opens whose maps to $S'$ are quasi-affine and whose pullbacks agree under the canonical datum. Restrict that datum to each open. The equality of inverse-image opens makes inclusion into $P$ compatible with transport; the identity and cocycle equations are restrictions of those on $P$.

source.place: Theorem 4.1 proof, invariant quasi-affine neighbourhoods, pp.17-21

proof.text: Each restricted datum is effective by [lem-trf-quasi-affine-fpqc-effective-descent], since $p$ is fpqc and $U_i\to S'$ is quasi-affine. The opens cover $P$ and their inclusions intertwine the canonical transport, exactly as required by [lem-pd-effective-invariant-open-cover]. That lemma glues their effective models to a scheme $X\to S$ and an isomorphism $P\simeq X\times_SS'$ inducing the canonical datum. This is where the local charts are assembled into the descended scheme.

The cartesian projection $P\to X$ is invariant under its canonical datum. Therefore [lem-pd-fpqc-representability-descent] identifies $h_X$ with $F$. In particular $Y\simeq X\times_ST$. Descent along $p$ also makes $X\to S$ locally of finite presentation. On each affine presentation, a finitely presented algebra is generated by its finitely many displayed variables, so this morphism is locally of finite type. Since $S$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] gives that $X$ is locally Noetherian.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.1, p.54; Stacks 02KY and 01T6, to establish the locally Noetherian target needed in Proposition 4.1.3

proof.text: Let $u:Y\to X$ be the projection. It is integral by base change of $q$ and is an fpqc cover by base change, hence surjective. Its underlying fibres are finite for a separate reason. For an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$, integrality makes $u^{-1}W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ an affine open of $Y$; $B$ is Noetherian because $Y$ is locally Noetherian. For $x\in W$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p\subset A$, the fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. Its ring is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian], and integral over the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by integrality under base change. The integral-extension dimension inequality makes its dimension at most zero. The zero-dimensional Noetherian scheme lemma now makes its point set finite (also for a zero fibre ring). Thus $u$ satisfies the finite-fibre condition without inferring it directly from base-change stability of finite underlying fibres.

source.place: Corollary 3.8, p.15, verification of its fibre hypothesis; Stacks integral base change and Noetherian fibre argument

proof.text: For any finite subset $E\subseteq|X|$, Step 6 makes $E'=u^{-1}(E)$ finite. Property (FA) for $Y$ puts $E'$ in an affine open of $Y$. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-finite-fibre-affine-neighbourhood-transfer] to $u$ and $E$: $X$ is locally Noetherian by Step 5, and $u$ is integral, surjective and has finite underlying fibres by Step 6. Its reverse implication supplies an affine open of $X$ containing $E$. This proves property (FA) for $X$. For $E=\varnothing$ the empty affine open is allowed.

source.place: Corollary 3.8, p.15; Anantharaman Proposition 4.1.3, p.55 (scan OCR 4.1.5)

proof.text: Assume additionally that $Y\to T$ is flat, separated and of finite presentation. Apply fpqc descent along the original cover $q:T\to S$ to the now existing scheme morphism $X\to S$. The cited flatness, separatedness, local finite-presentation and quasi-compactness descent statements give each of those four properties. Separatedness makes the diagonal a closed immersion; on an affine target chart its inverse image is a closed subscheme of an affine scheme and is affine, hence quasi-compact. Thus $X\to S$ is quasi-separated. By the definition of finite presentation (local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness), it is of finite presentation. All three requested properties therefore descend.

proof_origin.place: Expansion of the integral orbit criterion (Theorem 4.1, pp.16-21), using its invariant-chart output and Corollary 3.8, p.15, together with Stacks fpqc descent. Sources read online; local archival copies WANTED in report.md.

split_report.summary: Eight-step split. Three statement-only prerequisites isolate finite orbit images, the invariant quasi-affine neighbourhood transfer (no effectivity conclusion), and reflection of an affine neighbourhood of a specified finite set. Existing quasi-affine effectiveness and invariant-open gluing construct the representing scheme. The post-effectivity fibre check uses Noetherian fibre rings, not the invalid base-change claim for finite underlying fibres. Statement unchanged; property descent uses scheme-specific statements.

tool_uses.why: Step 4 uses effectiveness for an arbitrary quasi-affine morphism and singleton fpqc cover, as a generic scheme-descent theorem; the unit has no replacement effectiveness statement for these charts.
Step 4 glues effective restricted data on an invariant open covering, without any Picard-specific hypotheses; no node of this unit supplies this general gluing statement.
Step 5 identifies the effective scheme with the original fpqc set sheaf by its cartesian invariant model; this is general sheaf descent, not a Picard route.
Steps 1, 5 and 8 descend local finite presentation between existing scheme morphisms; this generic permanence result does not replace the integral effectivity argument.
Step 6 takes Noetherianity of a localization and quotient describing a fibre ring; this general commutative algebra fact is not supplied by the unit.
Step 6 bounds the dimension of a ring integral over a residue field; this generic integral-extension theorem is not a theorem about the unit route.
Step 6 uses finiteness of the underlying space of a zero-dimensional Noetherian scheme, as a general topological algebraic geometry fact.
Step 8 applies generic flatness descent to the constructed scheme, with no effectivity assumed in obtaining that scheme.
Step 8 applies generic separatedness descent to the constructed scheme; it does not change the route for constructing the scheme.
Step 8 applies generic quasi-compactness descent as one defining part of finite presentation; the unit supplies no separate general permanence lemma.
